scams.name: Palma Airport (PMI) & Port Taxi Overcharge
scams.description:
Palma de Mallorca Airport (PMI) is the third-busiest in Spain by passenger volume, handling massive summer traffic from the UK, Germany, and Scandinavia. The legitimate licensed taxi fare to central Palma is €20–€30 on the meter, and to El Arenal or the cruise port approximately €25–€35. Unofficial operators at the rank, particularly during peak summer arrivals, quote 'fixed prices' of €50–€70 with no meter. confirms: 'Palma center to the airport is usually less than €30 each way, so you won't be more than this.'

Traveler reports captures the 2025 summer crunch (German-language thread discussing 3-person-per-taxi allocations during luggage-heavy arrivals)...

For older cruise passengers and summer-package travelers arriving at PMI, the practical defense lives at the official meter. Use the licensed metered taxi rank or pre-book Cabify at the airport — refusing every fixed-price airport-curb quote above 30 euros to Palma center, and ignoring private-transfer touts at the cruise port. iving with luggage, the practical defense: (1) use the licensed yellow taxis at PMI arrivals (queue at Terminal A); (2) confirm the approximate fare range before boarding (€20–€30 to Palma center, €25–€35 to cruise port or El Arenal); (3) insist on the meter and photograph the taxi plate number; (4) Cabify operates in Mallorca with app-regulated fares and digital receipts — the strongest defense for older travelers; (5) avoid any driver who approaches inside the terminal rather than waiting at the taxi rank.
scams.avoidance: Use licensed yellow taxis at PMI arrivals queue at Terminal A Confirm approximate fare range before boarding: €20–€30 to Palma center, €25–€35 to cruise port or El Arenal Insist on the meter and photograph the taxi plate number from the rear windscreen Use Cabify app for app-regulated fares with digital receipts (Uber does not operate in Mallorca) Avoid any driver who approaches inside the terminal rather than waiting at the taxi rank
scams.location: Palma de Mallorca Airport (PMI) taxi rank, Cruise port pickup zones, nightlife-district return rides from El Arenal and Magaluf
scams.tldr: PMI airport-curb taxis quote fixed-price 40-60 euros for the 8-km Palma center run that should cost 20-30 metered, and Palma cruise-port hotels push private-transfer 70+ euros over the licensed 15-20 euro metered taxi.

scams.name: Palma Old Town & Cathedral (La Seu) Pickpockets
scams.description:
Traveler reports captures the local view: 'Yes, pretty much every tourist capital has pickpockets. Some even come here just for the summer' — the seasonal crews rotate between Mallorca, Barcelona, and the Costa del Sol. gives the comparative: 'In Mallorca when more touristic and full of people the more of a chance you'll get robbed, beaches like, playa' and Plaça Major concentrate the risk. gives the reassuring framing: 'Aside from pickpockets, it's very safe. To be fair, I can't think of any European cities (especially touristy' that are pickpocket-free.

The Palma-specific risk zones: (1) the Cathedral (La Seu) ticket queue and immediate surroundings during cruise-ship mornings (typically 10 AM–12 PM); (2) Paseo del Born evening terraces during summer; (3) Plaça Major's outdoor crafts market crowd; (4) Santa Catalina district nightlife on Friday and Saturday evenings; (5) Passeig Marítim waterfront promenade during cruise-excursion unloading. gives the 2025 defensive rule: 'The only thing about safety is: Be aware that at very crowded places, like at many tourist attractions, pickpo' ckets work.

For older cruise passengers on a Palma day visit, the practical defense lives in front-of-body bag posture. Wear a zipped crossbody bag in front through the Cathedral La Seu queue and Old Town narrow lanes, keeping phone in zipped inner pocket and refusing every photo-help or directions approach in cathedral-queue density. cal posture: (1) zipped crossbody bag in front during any old-town walking; (2) phone in zipped inner pocket — never back pocket or outer backpack; (3) split valuables: €20 + one card in front pocket; passport + backup card locked in cruise cabin or hotel safe; (4) avoid lingering at the Cathedral queue during 10 AM–12 PM cruise-peak; visit at 2–4 PM when cruise groups have left; (5) file denuncia at Policía Nacional Palma (Calle Simó Ballester 1, +34 971 225 500) within 48 hours for insurance.
scams.avoidance: Wear zipped crossbody bag in front during all old-town walking Never place phone or wallet in back pocket or outer backpack compartment Split valuables: €20 + one card in front pocket; passport + backup in cabin/hotel safe Visit Cathedral at 2–4 PM to avoid 10 AM–12 PM cruise-peak crowd File denuncia at Policía Nacional Palma (+34 971 225 500) within 48 hours for insurance
scams.location: Palma Cathedral (La Seu) queue, Plaça Major, Paseo del Born, Passeig Marítim, Santa Catalina district nightlife, cruise-ship-day crowds in old town
scams.tldr: Palma's old town has a documented pickpocket problem that intensifies during cruise-ship-day crowds and summer peak.

scams.name: El Arenal / Magaluf Beach & Nightlife Phone Theft
scams.description:
massive summer volumes of UK, German, and Scandinavian tourists, dense nightlife, and a pickpocket/phone-theft problem that has become organized and persistent. is a named-anchor 2025 victim account: 'I know this scam and I'm not clicking anything. Is there anything I can do at this point, given that the phone' — the victim's iPhone was stolen at El Arenal and tracked via Find My to the scammer's location in Palma, who then sent phishing 'unlock your iPhone' messages as a follow-up scam. The full scam sequence: steal phone at beach/nightclub; lock phone via iCloud-delete attempt; phish the victim with fake 'Apple unlock' messages.

Traveler reports confirms the El Arenal concentration. gives the 2025 framing: 'Try not to be scammed, so many scams towards tourists, usually by ot' her tourists or seasonal crews operating specifically at package-tourism beaches. The nightlife variant: crowded Magaluf clubs during 11 PM–3 AM use the dance-floor crush for phone and wallet lifts, with partial drunk tourists making recovery unlikely.

For older travelers on a Palma cruise or resort stay who venture to El Arenal or Magaluf, the practical defense lives in nightlife avoidance. Skip Magaluf and El Arenal nightlife strips entirely if you are 60+, and if you must visit, leave phone and wallet at the resort safe and bring only 50 euros cash plus a decoy phone. ture to El Arenal during the day or Santa Catalina in the evening, the practical defense: (1) rent a beachfront locker at the chiringuito (€3–€5 per session) for phone and wallet during swims; (2) use a waterproof pouch around your neck for phone and one card only; (3) if your phone is stolen, immediately activate Find My iPhone's Lost Mode rather than attempting to wipe — wipe attempts may be exploited for the phishing follow-up; (4) do not respond to any 'Apple unlock' or 'iCloud recovery' messages after a theft; (5) file denuncia at Policía Nacional Palma (+34 971 225 500) within 24 hours.
scams.avoidance: Rent beachfront locker at El Arenal chiringuito (€3–€5 per session) for valuables during swims Use waterproof pouch around your neck for phone and one card only during swims If phone is stolen, activate Find My iPhone's Lost Mode — do not attempt full wipe Ignore any 'Apple unlock' or 'iCloud recovery' messages after a theft — all are phishing File denuncia at Policía Nacional Palma (+34 971 225 500) within 24 hours for insurance
scams.location: El Arenal beach strip, Magaluf nightlife district, Playa de Palma, club exit crowds, beachfront cafeterias and chiringuitos
scams.tldr: massive summer volumes of UK, German, and Scandinavian tourists, dense nightlife, and a pickpocket/phone-theft problem that has become organized and persistent.

scams.name: Fake Speeding-Ticket Letters for Rental Cars
scams.description:
After a Mallorca rental-car holiday, victims receive official-looking 'speeding ticket' letters in the post at their home address in the UK or Germany, claiming to show their rental car exceeding a speed limit on a Mallorca road. The letter demands immediate payment (typically €60–€150) via a European bank transfer or card payment to a 'collection agency' that is not connected to the Spanish traffic authority (Dirección General de Tráfico). for the scam: 'It's a pretty good scam as it has all the correct details regarding the hire car and my details, but the pictu' re of the vehicle is not clearly from a Spanish traffic camera and the demand routes to a non-DGT account.

The sophistication comes from information that looks insider: correct rental-car number plate, correct driver name, correct rental-pickup dates. Scammers obtain this through one of several vectors: (1) corrupt employees at rental-car companies who sell bulk datasets; (2) hacked rental-company email systems; (3) reused personal data from prior Mallorca traffic tickets that were actually paid. It's the re' sort that the fake-ticket operators work in tandem with a real-ticket pattern to confuse victims.

For older travelers returning from a Mallorca rental-car holiday, the practical defense lives in DGT verification. For any post-return speeding-ticket letter, verify directly via DGT.es or +34 060 — never click email links — and refuse all urgent-payment-100-euros-to-avoid-surcharge demands as fraud built on leaked rental records. iday, the practical defense: (1) genuine Spanish DGT speeding tickets are issued by registered post or via the official Boletín Oficial del Estado, not by private collection agencies; (2) pay only via the official DGT website (dgt.es) or the designated bank; (3) verify any received ticket by calling DGT directly (+34 060 within Spain, +34 902 101 062 internationally); (4) if the letter demands payment to a non-DGT account, file a complaint with Policía Nacional in Mallorca (+34 971 225 500) and Action Fraud (in the UK) or your home-country fraud authority; (5) do not pay until verification; DGT will not suspend your license for a 60-day verification delay.
scams.avoidance: Pay genuine Spanish DGT tickets only via dgt.es (official) or the designated bank Verify any received ticket by calling DGT directly: +34 060 (within Spain) or +34 902 101 062 (international) File a complaint with Policía Nacional Palma (+34 971 225 500) and your home-country fraud authority if scam-suspected Do not pay until verification — DGT will not suspend your license for a 60-day verification delay Retain your rental-car pickup and return documents as reference for disputed fines
scams.location: By post at your home address after a Mallorca rental-car trip, email to the email address used for the rental booking
scams.tldr: Mallorca rental-car holders receive fake Spanish DGT speeding-ticket 100-200 euro letters or emails post-return, built on leaked rental records, pressuring urgent-payment-to-avoid-surcharge — verify only at DGT.es or +34 060.

scams.name: Cruise Excursion Overcharge & 'Exclusive' Shore-Tour Packages
scams.description:
Palma is one of the Western Mediterranean's top cruise destinations, with 1.4 million cruise passengers annually on ships like the Royal Caribbean Oasis, Costa Cruises, and MSC. Cruise lines sell 'Palma highlights' shore excursions at €80–€150 per person, marketing 'exclusive' access to the Cathedral, Bellver Castle, and a coastal drive. The same experience arranged independently via Cabify (€15 taxi into Palma center) + self-guided Cathedral visit (€10 at catedraldemallorca.org) + walk along Passeig del Born costs under €30 per person. ETA - the most I've ever driven in a day was driving 18 hours r' — meaning cruise-excursion refunds for canceled or altered tours are notoriously difficult to obtain.

gives the veteran-cruiser's view: 'tour/excursion or you are brave enough to jump into a taxi and you don't care about aggressive taxi driver' s — meaning Palma is easy enough for an independent day but cruise-line marketing creates the impression you need the package. gives the local perspective on one specific excursion scam: 'We got an 80€ ticket for driving somewhere we were not supposed to go-huge scam if you ask me, but would still' visit again.

For older cruise passengers on a Palma day, the practical alternative is to skip the cruise excursion booking. Skip cruise-line shore-excursion packages at 120-250 euros per person, and DIY via taxi (20-30 euros to La Seu) or the L1 bus from cruise port, with the same monuments at 15-30 euro entry total. ternative: (1) skip the cruise-line Palma Cathedral/Bellver Castle excursion at €80–€150 per person; (2) take the cruise-provided port-to-town shuttle (free or €5) or a Cabify ride (€15) to central Palma; (3) visit the Cathedral at catedraldemallorca.org (€10); (4) walk the old town (Plaça Major, Paseo del Born) at your pace; (5) return to the port via Cabify or shuttle. Total independent cost: €30–€50 per person. If you want a guided tour, book a paid small-group tour on GetYourGuide (€35–€50) rather than the cruise-line excursion — same content, half the price, flexible timing.
scams.avoidance: Skip cruise-line Palma excursions; plan an independent day at one-third the cost Use the cruise-provided port shuttle (free or €5) or a Cabify ride (€15) to central Palma Book Cathedral tickets at catedraldemallorca.org (€10 admission) If you want a guided tour, use GetYourGuide or Tiqets small-group tours (€35–€50) rather than cruise-line packages Walk the old town (Plaça Major, Paseo del Born, Santa Catalina) independently — no queues, full day flexibility
scams.location: Palma Cruise Port hand-off zones, cruise-ship excursion desks pushing 'Palma highlights' at €80–€150 per person, independent tour touts near the terminal
scams.tldr: Cruise-line Palma shore-excursion packages cost 120-250 euros per person for what's a 20-30 euro taxi to La Seu plus 15-30 euro monument entries — DIY saves 70-200 euros per person, and the same monuments are walkable from the cruise port.

scams.name: Palma Short-Term Rental & Airbnb Booking Fraud
scams.description:
Palma's rental-accommodation fraud follows the pattern of San Sebastián, Valencia, and Córdoba: tourism-driven demand combined with housing-supply pressure creates the conditions for scams that specifically target travelers looking for apartment-style stays longer than a hotel week. 'We are a few tourists visiting Palma for the long weekend. We are in an airbnb' and suspected fraud when the host tried to redirect payment off-platform.

The pattern across Palma: (1) listing at 20–30% below comparable hotel rates on Idealista or Facebook Marketplace; (2) 'landlord' asks for a deposit plus first-month rent via Bizum or bank transfer before any viewing; (3) payment clears, 'landlord' disappears; (4) or the alternate: a real property is double-booked to multiple travelers simultaneously...

For older travelers considering an apartment stay in Palma longer than a hotel weekend, the protective playbook lives in platform-only payment. Book only through Airbnb or VRBO with platform-verified payment, refusing Bizum, Western Union, or wire transfers and verifying the Mallorca Tourist Registration (ETV) number before any deposit. onger than a weekend, the protective playbook: (1) book only through Airbnb or Booking.com with platform-verified payment and cancellation protection; (2) for Idealista listings, demand a video call with the apartment visible before any deposit; (3) reverse-image-search listing photos on Google Images before paying; (4) refuse Western Union, Bizum, or cryptocurrency payment for any accommodation deposit; (5) on arrival, briefly check common rooms for hidden cameras (smoke detectors, alarm clocks, tissue boxes are common hiding spots per 2025 traveler reports reports); (6) file a denuncia at Policía Nacional Palma (+34 971 225 500) immediately if defrauded.
scams.avoidance: Book only through Airbnb or Booking.com with platform-verified payment and cancellation protection For Idealista listings, demand a video call with the apartment visible before any deposit Reverse-image-search listing photos on Google Images before paying Refuse Bizum, Western Union, or cryptocurrency payment for any accommodation deposit On arrival, briefly check common rooms for hidden cameras (smoke detectors, alarm clocks, tissue boxes are common hiding spots per 2025 traveler reports)
scams.location: Online — Airbnb, Booking, Idealista Palma listings, private WhatsApp referrals during peak summer season
scams.tldr: Palma Idealista, Kleinanzeigen, and Facebook Marketplace apartment listings demand Bizum/wire-transfer deposits sight-unseen — verify the Mallorca Tourist Registration (ETV) number before any payment, and book only on Airbnb or VRBO with platform card.
